Behavior.DamageRecipe_13529_regeneration.reason: Rage of Purphoros's regeneration prohibition should end at cleanup. A legally pumped Wall of Bone survives damage and cleanup, returns to 1/4 with zero damage, then activates regeneration during a subsequent destruction window. This dedicated timing case retains real mana payment/source exile and intentionally ends stack1; no target is fabricated or requeued. Oracle assertions retained; production fix deferred.

Oracle makes the not-monstrous condition a resolution condition and prints no activation limit. After the first activation resolves, the creature is monstrous and has sufficient mana for another activation. That activation is legal, pays its printed cost, and adds no further counters on resolution. The shared monstrosity helper incorrectly returns false from EVENT_CAN_ACTIVATE when SF2_MONSTROUS is set (theros.c:497). Oracle assertions retained; production fix deferred.

Oracle prints no once-per-turn limit on this activated ability. While the first activation is pending, controller1 may pay the printed cost and activate it again; the first resolution makes the source monstrous and adds counters, and the later resolution adds none. The shared monstrosity helper instead sets GAA_ONCE_PER_TURN for controller1 (theros.c:570; defs.h:1712), records usage in generic_activated_ability (functions.c:15592), and rejects the next query (functions.c:15226). Oracle assertions retained; production fix deferred.

Oracle prints {1}, Sacrifice an artifact as the activation cost. Actual activation must spend one mana as well as sacrificing the artifact, and is unavailable with no mana. card_syndicate_trafficker delegates its availability and activation to generic_husk (kaladesh.c:3004–3023); generic_husk explicitly tests and charges zero mana (functions.c:4010–4021). Successful cases retain actual artifact sacrifice, counter growth, indestructibility, cleanup, pending/source-loss and replay receipts; these exact failures are omitted mana payments. The insufficient-mana case fails the actual availability query before an activation can proceed. Oracle assertions retained; production fix deferred.

Behavior.CounterExtensionRecipe_5072_kic.reason: Prohibit targets a spell without a mana-value restriction; its mana-value test determines whether that spell is countered on resolution. The fatal require-can-cast guard preserves the legal Oracle expectation and stops before invalid follow-up interactions. Independently source/log reviewed; production fix deferred.

Behavior.GraveyardExileRecipe_7958_parti.reason: Oracle resolves the remaining legal selected cards when only the first target leaves the graveyard. A real Reclaim moves that first low-position card to its owner's library before the parent resolves. Decompose and Shred Memory call legacy validate_target_from_grave, storing raw positions plus IID. Its documented lower-card-removal limitation invalidates all shifted remaining targets, leaving them in the graveyard. Preserve the remaining targets' exile identities, counts and multiplicities. Independently source/log reviewed; no response-helper artifact or production fix.

Behavior.AttackValueTriggerRecipe_11729_.reason: Riddlekeeper must trigger once for each attacking creature: two opposing declared attackers must mill four cards in total, even when no combat damage is dealt. Its handler calls store_attackers with DAT_SEPARATE_TRIGGERS, but calls dat_ability with only the optional/mandatory resolution mode. resolve_declare_attackers_trigger therefore returns the aggregate count of two once, and dat_ability invokes EVENT_DAT_ABILITY once; card_riddlekeeper ignores that count and mills a fixed two. Both controllers actually mill two rather than four, leaving ten library cards instead of eight and three graveyard cards instead of five, with the exact top-card/multiplicity mismatches preserved. Current native batch and isolated captures have twelve matching zone assertions and no unconsumed choices, harness errors or crashes. Source-grounded ordinary rules defect; production fix deferred; paired Wasm validation follows baseline integration.

With no optional acceptance queued, the engine skips the required draw(s), leaving the hand short and the library unadvanced. These cases retain the correct draw, zone and library expectations; production correction is deferred.

Correct cast-count-derived counters and power/toughness expectations remain unchanged; production correction is deferred.

The fixture actually casts the enchantment with its separate printed casting budget, casts the fresh recipient, then explicitly establishes the activation test pool. After the real legal land sacrifice, activation incorrectly spends one red mana per activation. This case records actual totals[79] versus Oracle80 and red[9] versus10. Its EVENT_ACTIVATE passes MANACOST_R(1), introducing this charge; exact cost receipts retain the correct printed zero mana. Human actual land choice precedes the distinct effect target; AI chooses legal owned Plains automatically, without a forced victim. Non-cost Haste/recipient/zone/snapshot receipts remain correct, with no other fixture or harness failure. Confirmed in the engine18 remaining73 native batch and its actual isolated recheck. No Wasm claim yet. Correct zero-mana Oracle, actual inputs and decoded body unchanged; production fix deferred.
